task.sonnet_answer: The 2026 U.S. Women's Open is scheduled to be held at Riviera Country Club in Pacific Palisades, California. Riviera Country Club is historically associated with Ben Hogan, who won there multiple times and gave the course its nickname 'Hogan's Alley.'

answer:
The 2026 U.S. Women's Open, held at the Riviera Country Club in Pacific Palisades, California, featured notable players such as Nelly Korda, who won the tournament, and runners-up Charley Hull and Gaby López. The field included players who gained entry through qualifying events and those exempt from qualifying due to various criteria, such as recent major champions and leading players in the Women's World Golf Rankings. 

FINAL: Nelly Korda won; Charley Hull and Gaby López were runners-up.

[en:2026 U.S. Women's Open] The 2026 U.S. Women's Open presented by Ally was the 81st U.S. Women's Open, held June 4–7 at Riviera Country Club in Pacific Palisades, California. Nelly Korda won her fourth major title (and second consecutive), one stroke ahead of runners-up Charley Hull and Gaby López. [en:2026 US Open – Women's singles] Elena Rybakina defeated two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka in the final, 6–4, 5–7, 6–2 to win the women's singles tennis title at the 2026 US Open. It was her third major title (and second of the season, having also won the Australian Open) and 14th WTA Tour title overall. Rybakina was the sixth women's singles player (since 1988) to win both hardcourt majors in the same year, with Sabalenka and Rybakina also being the first pair of women's singles players to contest both hardcourt major finals in the same year since Steffi Graf and Arantxa Sánchez Vicario in 1994. This was also the first US Open final contested by the top two seeds since 2013. Rybakina attained the world No. 1 singles ranking for the first time by reaching the semifinals, becoming the 30th player to attain the top ranking and the first Kazakhstani player to achieve a world No. 1 ranking in any discipline. Sabalenka, Jessica Pegula, and Coco Gauff were also in contention for the top ranking at the beginning of the tournament. Aged 46, Venus Williams was the oldest woman to compete in the US Open singles main draw since Renée Richards in 1981, after receiving a wildcard into the main draw. Starting at 12:13 AM, the first-round match between Williams and Sofia Kenin set the record for the latest start in tournament history, surpassing the previous record (12:08 AM) set by the third-round match between Sabalenka and Ekaterina Alexandrova in 2024. Zheng Qinwen was the first qualifier to reach the quarterfinals since Emma Raducanu in 2021. All of the top four seeds reached the semifinals for the first time at the US Open since 1975 and at any major since the 2009 Wimbledon Championships.
